title: Improving the UI of a 4x Strategy Game
author: certaintyisuncertain
selftext:
I've been working on this multi-player 4x strategy game where everyone takes 1 turn a day and posting the progress here for awhile.

It started as a different game called House & Dominion that was up on [Itch.io](http://Itch.io) that some of you tried. The cost of having LLM's run the "court" scenarios and personalities of the characters was too expensive (and jenky). I think there's something to revisit there, but the part of the game everyone seemed most interested in (and me too) was the actual kingdom-building.

So that's the game now, totally reworked for that.

I posted a "beta" (which is kind of funny, probably should be pre-alpha, i don't know) video a few weeks ago here and it picked up some new players but also some good feedback on the UI looking too genericly "AI" -- that was totally right.

So I spent the last 2 weeks, a little bit focused on gameplay as more players joined. Also added a discord as requested. But a lot was focused on the UI.

First, I took screenshots from Civ & Total War & Crusader Kings (which made me realize nobody really had great UI for these types of games... it's all kind of spreadsheets plastered with some "parchment paper" looks), but that made it a little better.

Then I worked through all the menus and told Claude exactly what to compact and where and how to make some of it more visual than just text.

A big thing was instead of having big scrolling menus with sub-sections, I made all the sub-sections tabs. Which Claude still wanted to put too many words on it. So I had to "talk it into" just sticking with icons and letting the player learn what those icons mean.

If you want to come join the game, it's running in the shared world. I'm having fun, seems like the other players are too. We just started the discord, which should help build up some more community, and I'm very actively listening to product roadmap feedback.   
  
[https://onceadaydynasty.com/](https://onceadaydynasty.com/) *(totally free to play, for right now just really having fun with it and without the LLM's in-game, it's cheap enough I can afford to run it without monetization for now and for a long time)*

If you check it out, I'm eager to hear more feedback on the UI.  Especially anything specific is helpful!
